question.prompt: Right triangle \(ABC\) has side lengths \(BC = 6,\) \(AC = 8,\) and \(AB = 10.\) A circle centered at \(O\) is tangent to line \(BC\) at \(B\) and passes through \(A.\) A circle centered at \(P\) is tangent to line \(AC\) at \(A\) and passes through \(B.\) What is \(OP?\)

solutions.title: Locate the centers
solutions.explanation:
A radius to a tangency point is perpendicular to the tangent, so placing the legs on the coordinate axes fixes one coordinate of each center.

Take
\[
C=(0,0),\qquad B=(6,0),\qquad A=(0,8).
\]
Because \(OB\perp BC\), write \(O=(6,k)\). Both \(A\) and \(B\) lie on this circle, so \(OA=OB\). Squaring the distances gives
\[
36+(k-8)^2=k^2,
\]
which simplifies to \(100-16k=0\). Thus
\[
O=\left(6,\frac{25}{4}\right).
\]
Similarly, \(PA\perp AC\), so write \(P=(h,8)\). The equal radii \(PB=PA\) give
\[
(h-6)^2+64=h^2,
\]
so \(100-12h=0\) and
\[
P=\left(\frac{25}{3},8\right).
\]
The horizontal and vertical differences between the centers are \(\frac73\) and \(\frac74\). Therefore
\[
OP=\sqrt{\left(\frac73\right)^2+\left(\frac74\right)^2}
=7\sqrt{\frac{16+9}{144}}
=\boxed{\frac{35}{12}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Use the shared perpendicular bisector
solutions.explanation:
Both circles pass through \(A\) and \(B\), so their centers lie on the same perpendicular bisector. Similar triangles will locate them along that line.

Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AB\). Then
\[
AM=BM=5.
\]
The equal radii \(OA=OB\) and \(PA=PB\) put \(O\) and \(P\) on the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\), so \(M,O,P\) are collinear and \(MO\perp AB\).

The tangent-radius property gives \(BO\parallel CA\) and \(AP\parallel CB\). Each circle lies on the side of its tangent containing the other given vertex. Thus \(O\) and \(P\) are both on the side of \(AB\) opposite \(C\), and hence on the same perpendicular ray from \(M\).

The parallel lines give \(\angle MBO=\angle CAB\). Since \(\angle BMO=\angle ACB=90^\circ\), triangles \(BMO\) and \(ACB\) are similar. Therefore
\[
\frac{MO}{BC}=\frac{BM}{AC},
\qquad
MO=6\cdot\frac58=\frac{15}{4}.
\]
Likewise, \(\angle MAP=\angle ABC\), so the right triangles \(AMP\) and \(BCA\) are similar. This gives
\[
\frac{MP}{AC}=\frac{AM}{BC},
\qquad
MP=8\cdot\frac56=\frac{20}{3}.
\]
Because both centers lie on the same ray from \(M\) and \(MP>MO\),
\[
OP=MP-MO=\frac{20}{3}-\frac{15}{4}
=\boxed{\frac{35}{12}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
